title: Knowledge grounding: which data can a Copilot Studio agent answer from?
summary: Hold: the two maker-setting paths omit the Settings page needed to reach Generative AI. The billing rates, Dataverse update operation and knowledge-source restrictions are supported; the introductory navigation also needs its standard-harness scope made explicit.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Knowledge sources ground an agent's responses in enterprise content.
claims.quote: Knowledge sources ground your agent's responses in enterprise data.

claims.where: What it is: opening paragraph
claims.claim: Makers add knowledge sources on an agent's Knowledge page.
claims.quote: You can incorporate knowledge at the agent level, in the **Knowledge** page
claims.fix: Begin the navigation sentence 'For agents powered by the standard harness, makers add them'. The Microsoft Copilot harness instead uses the Knowledge button on the Build tab, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/knowledge-add-existing-copilot; this qualification avoids presenting the older navigation as universal.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: semantic index; controls[4].note

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Upload files > SharePoint storage
claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: When you use **Upload files > SharePoint** as a knowledge source, your files are stored in Dataverse, where they're processed and indexed for use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Upload files > SharePoint capacity
claims.claim: SharePoint-upload knowledge files consume Dataverse data storage.
claims.quote: Your files and folders remain in Dataverse, so they do consume data storage.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers stay possible
claims.claim: Disabling Allow ungrounded responses does not prevent combining model knowledge with retrieved information.
claims.quote: The agent's underlying model might still incorporate general knowledge when it combines this knowledge with information it retrieves from knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: Disabling Allow ungrounded responses blocks responses from turns that used no source or tool.
claims.quote: When you turn off this setting, the agent blocks any response generated in a turn where it didn't use a knowledge source or tool.

claims.where: Risks and limits: conversation-history follow-up
claims.claim: A follow-up answered from conversation history without another source or tool call can be blocked.
claims.quote: the agent might decide it already has enough context from previous turns to answer the follow-up question, without needing to call another tool or knowledge source, so the response is blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: in-text citations
claims.claim: With ungrounded responses disabled, a knowledge-source answer needs an in-text citation.
claims.quote: When you turn off **Allow ungrounded responses**, the agent returns an answer from a knowledge source only when the answer includes an in-text citation to that source.

claims.where: Risks and limits: correct but uncited answers
claims.claim: The agent can withhold a correct source-derived answer if its citation is missing.
claims.quote: Occasionally, the model generates a correct answer from a knowledge source but doesn't include a citation for it. When that happens, the agent withholds the answer and responds as though it didn't find any information.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The Documents setting is narrow
claims.claim: Disallowing Documents uploads blocks only local file uploads.
claims.quote: Configuring **Documents** knowledge source to not allow uploads only prevents local file uploads.

claims.where: Risks and limits: SharePoint and OneDrive restriction
claims.claim: Disallowing Documents does not block SharePoint or OneDrive uploads; those require restricting SharePoint + OneDrive.
claims.quote:
It doesn't prevent makers from adding files from SharePoint or OneDrive.

To not allow uploads from SharePoint or OneDrive, configure **SharePoint + OneDrive** to not allow access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Uploaded files skip per-user checks
claims.claim: The file upload method allows anyone with permission to the agent to access the file.
claims.quote: The upload files method allows anyone with permission to the agent to access the file.

claims.where: Risks and limits: SharePoint credential checks
claims.claim: SharePoint knowledge checks the user's credentials before providing file-based responses.
claims.quote: With SharePoint, the user's credentials are verified to ensure they have permission to access the file before providing responses.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off; What to check
claims.claim: The configuration documentation says disabling Dataverse search removes the index within 12 hours.
claims.quote: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes the index within 12 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: uploaded-file sources; controls[2].governs
claims.claim: Uploaded-file knowledge relies on Dataverse search and stops returning indexed results when it is off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: SharePoint or OneDrive upload sources
claims.claim: Turning Dataverse search off also disables experiences using OneDrive or SharePoint files added via upload.
claims.quote: any generative AI experience that relies on Dataverse, like uploaded files or using OneDrive or SharePoint files (via upload) in Microsoft Copilot Studio agents

claims.where: Risks and limits: rebuilding the index
claims.claim: A fresh Dataverse index sync can take an hour or more for average-sized organizations.
claims.quote: If you turn on Dataverse search after it's been off for 12 hours, it creates a fresh index that needs to go through a full sync. Syncing can take an hour or more for average size organizations

claims.where: Risks and limits: rebuilding for large organizations
claims.claim: Dataverse index sync can take a couple of days for large organizations.
claims.quote: Syncing can take an hour or more for average size organizations, and a couple of days for large organizations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: multi-day caveat; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft also cautions that index removal or provisioning can take multiple days depending on indexed volume.
claims.quote: Index removal (or provisioning) can take multiple days to be completed, depending on the amount of Dataverse search consumption.
